newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease in continued correction.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease in continued correction.

text.p: Istanbul shares dropped slightly in weaker volume on Friday in continued correction, but recovered from lows on mild support that emerged after Thursday's 3.7 percent plunge, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 closed down 361.74 points, or 0.47 percent at 76,210.51 after rebounding from an afternoon low of 75,831. Trade volume dived to 12.08 trillion lira from 18.6 trillion on Thursday.
Brokers said the market struggled to keep the index at above the 76,000 mark where initial support was expected. The index twice recovered from slightly below 76,000.
"76,000 is an important level. If the market opens lower on Monday, the easing may continue towards 73,500-74,000 range," said Murat Emrali from Eczacibasi securities.
"But if it bottoms out at 76,000-76,500 and turns up, it will face resistance at 77,500 and then drift sideways for a while," he added.

Yesterday's plunge was the first major correction to the latest uptrend during which the index rocketed 22.7 percent from September 13 to Wednesday's sixth consecutive all-time high close of 79,511.82.
Over the week, the index lost 0.63 percent after last week's 7.15 percent jump.

Brokers said the market would be tuned to political developments early next week when the government will face an opposition challenge. The parliament will debate a censure motion against Prime Minister Erbakan on October 16 for his controversial trip to Libya last week.
"Players also did not want to take risks ahead of the weekend because of Wednesday's censure motion," said Mustafa Oral from Universal securities.
"The market will move according to estimates ahead of the parliamentary vote. If the result is not negative, the uptrend is likely to continue," he added.

Of the 223 shares traded, 87 declined, 63 advanced and 73 closed unchanged. The 85-share industrial index .ISEI firmed 0.17 percent to 82,240.43 while the 15-share financial index lost 1.95 percent to 70,277.46.
Top actives were utilities Kepez Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 84,000, Aktas Elektrik, steady at 59,000 lira and Cukurova Elektrik, down 1,000 lira at 74,000.
